title: Does a Heat Pump Actually Save Money?
summary: EnergySage 2026 guide: when heat pumps save money (warm climates, replacing oil/propane/resistance, hybrids, solar) and when gas in cold climates wins.

assertions.quote: Heat pumps are likely to save you money on heating and cooling, but it's not guaranteed.

verdicts.note: NREL's 2024 national simulation found 62-95% of households would see lower energy bills, depending on heat pump efficiency.

assertions.quote: The math all depends on individual circumstances: Your home, your climate, your local energy prices and policies
Heat pumps consistently save against propane, oil, and electric resistance heating almost everywhere.
If it rarely drops below freezing where you live, a heat pump is almost a no-brainer.
equipment and installation costs are lower—often barely more than a central AC alone.
Installing a heat pump often costs less than simply swapping in a new AC and furnace or boiler

verdicts.note: Some programs find parity, but NREL/LBNL 2024 put medium- and high-efficiency heat pumps well above a furnace-plus-AC replacement.

assertions.quote: If you live in a cold climate and currently have natural gas for heat, a heat pump will usually cost more to run
the wholesale cost of a cold-climate heat pump is roughly three times the cost of a basic furnace and twice the cost of a boiler.
Pairing a heat pump with rooftop solar is one of the most effective ways to offset that.
a hybrid system that automatically switches to the cheaper fuel at that crossover point can lower your annual energy costs.
heat pump payback periods are hard to pin down precisely—and that's not a cop-out.
